note: Scripture authority is the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0), bundled as library/data/bible/owb-am-b.json.gz and read offline (owb-am). Every Scripture quotation was re-quoted to it verbatim (founder decision, 2026-11-18: Amharic quotes OWB everywhere), replacing the 1962/2003 UBS wording and the translator-rendered Old Testament verses the first edition carried.

A `mined` row is a verbatim OWB span in that block: the whole verse, the shortest contiguous span carrying the quoted clause, or exact OWB pieces joined with '…'; verbatim recitations without quote marks count (Mark 3:13, Mark 3:28, 2 Pet 1:16, 1 Pet 1:21, Ps 68:18). The Heb 12:16-17 refrain that runs through the book is OWB's every time («በኋላ በረከቱን ለመውረስ በፈለገ ጊዜ እንደ ተመለሰ ታውቃላችሁ። በእንባ ቢለምንም ለንስሓ በር አላገኘም»), and Bunyan's 'place of repentance' in his own prose follows its «በር». Where Bunyan dwells on a quoted word the echo follows OWB: Mark 3:13 'whom he would' (የፈለጋቸውን), Ps 68:18 'the rebellious' (ካመፁብህም), John 6:37's «ከቶ» and «የሚመጣውን», 'yet there is room' (አሁንም ባዶ ስፍራዎች አሉ). John 10:35's 'the Scripture cannot be broken' quotes OWB's clause «ሊሻር የማይችል» inside Bunyan's sentence. Heb 6 and Heb 10:26 are joined with '…' where Bunyan runs them together ('It is impossible; there remains no more sacrifice for sin'). Citations follow the verse that holds the words: 'Come after me' Mark 1:17, 'Lord, Lord, open to us' Matt 25:11, 'This is for many days' quoted as OWB Dan 10:14.

`self_rendered` rows (each with a `why`) are allusions, bare citations and Bunyan's own wording woven around a verse; the voices he heard ('Thou art my love'; 'My grace is sufficient' without 'for thee', the lack he goes on to pray about; 'But I will not leave thee'; 'Return, return'); Ecclesiasticus 2:10, which OWB does not carry; and three places where his argument rests on an AV wording OWB does not have: Joel 3:21 'cleanse their blood' (OWB 'avenge'), Isa 26:19 'together with my dead body', and Job 21:14 turned into his own first-person prayer.
